items.title: VAST开源实时世界模型EdenLive！单消费级显卡、720P超24FPS
items.summary: 让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

extra.evidence: 让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界 据VAST介绍，EdenLive首次实现了在实时生成的前提下，同时完成任意参考输入、任意画风生成和长时连续运行。 具体来说，给它简化场景或参考视频，再配上目标首帧和提示词，就能沿着参考的布局与运动，持续生成写实、二次元等不同画风的精细画面。 在单张消费级显卡Nvidia RTX 5090上、720P条件下，5B模型的生成速度 超过24FPS ，还能持续生成分钟级画面。 据VAST介绍，从用户输入操作到对应画面出现，这套系统目前的端到端延迟为百毫秒级。 画面持续变化的同时，交互规则和世界状态由上游交互系统维护。系统接收玩家操作、更新状态，EdenLive再根据对应的参考画面，将这些变化实时呈现出来。 GPT-6 Astra 就是一个典型例子：它已经能够在Blender里搭建房屋，再将其转入Unreal Engine 5，形成可以进入、漫游的场景。 当AI能够搭建场景、设计交互玩法，如何让这些内容获得精细且实时的视觉表现，也就成为接下来需要解决的问题。 在这样的背景下，一条技术路线逐渐成为行业共识： 由交互系统维护底层状态和运行规则，再由生成模型负责视觉渲染 。 当时公开的Project Eden研究预览，已将 「状态维护与视觉渲染解耦」 作为核心设计。 如今，EdenLive作为这条路线的阶段性成果发布，并开放模型权重和推理代码，同步公开技术报告与端到端Demo。 代码： https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/EdenLive 技术报告： https://assets.vast-eden.ai/assets/edenlive/EdenLive-tech-report.pdf 开放权重： https://huggingface.co/VAST-AI/EdenLive EdenLive的核心价值，在于为简化场…

items.title: vllm-project/vllm v0.32.0

extra.evidence: # v0.32.0 ## Highlights This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)! * **Structured decisions and generic parsers**: the new `POST /v1/systemone` endpoint answers `choice`, `noul` and `score` questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on `Cloudflare/clef-omni` (#61064), `LiquidAI/d1-3B` (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new `hf` tool and reasoning parser (`--tool-call-parser hf`, `--reasoning-parser hf`) reads the checkpoint's `response_template`, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005). * **Low-precision KV cache everywhere**: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); `fp8_ds_mla` on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit `ultraquant_4bit` KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057). * **Model Runner V2**: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed…

items.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
items.summary: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the…

items.title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
items.summary: Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities. However, enabling multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information from complex, heterogeneous multimodal data remains a significant challenge as they move toward long-horizon tasks and lifelong settings. Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accumulated experience. We introduce a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory structured around two key questions: how multimodal information is formed and represented (Axis I, Formation and Representation), and how its management adapts with accumulated experience (Axis II, Memory Management). Axis I, Formation and Representation, characterizes what information is retained and how it is encoded (e.g., modality-specific embeddings, textual and structured records, latent and parametric representations) to support subsequent reasoning and action. Axis II, Memory Management, distinguishes three tiers: T1 Static Memory reuses fixed memory; T2 Dynamic Memory updates memory through a stable policy; and T3 Self-Evolving Memory updates memory through an evolving policy. Based on this framework, we synthesize recurring design patterns and derive principles for balancing source fide…

items.title: History Replays Itself: Unleashing Long-Context Capability in Linear Attention
items.summary: Linear attention promises the efficiency needed for long-context language modelling, yet its fixed-size recurrent state must simultaneously support ongoing computation and preserve information from an ever-growing history. This coupling has reinforced a prevailing view that the state's memory capacity defines the model's long-context capability. We challenge this presumed ceiling: \emph{recurrent computation need not bear the full burden of long-term storage}. We introduce NoteBank, a sparse episodic memory that archives selected text before future queries are known, uses the backbone's native features for writing and addressing, and reads retrieved evidence through its native forward computation via replay. This \emph{training-free, plug-and-play} interface requires no external embedding model, separately trained retriever, or separate neural reader. At one million tokens, it raises Gated DeltaNet's mean accuracy across six RULER retrieval tasks from 1.7% to 70.3%, with no observed significant retrieval degradation from 4K to 1M tokens. This recovery adds $\leqslant$0.025% to analytical FLOPs, with persistent context storage approximately 1/2,600 that of a Transformer's full MHA KV cache at matched width, depth, and precision. Experiments extend from three 1.3B recurrent backbones to Mamba-2-8B and post-trained Qwen3.5-9B, demonstrating gains on LongBench v1/v2 and MemoryAgentBench. Together, these results show that sparse evidence storage and native replay can substantiall…

items.title: MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization
items.summary: The Key-Value (KV) cache constitutes a dominant source of memory consumption during large language model (LLM) inference, particularly in long-context and complex reasoning scenarios. Existing KV cache quantization methods have explored different compression granularities, including layer-wise precision adjustment and token-level information preservation. In practical deployment, however, the key challenge is not merely compression, but how to allocate limited quantization resources among heterogeneous precision preservation strategies under a fixed KV cache memory budget. We propose MultiAlloc, a profiling-guided precision allocation framework for KV cache quantization that adaptively distributes limited quantization resources between layer-wise precision enhancement and token-wise preservation. MultiAlloc employs lightweight offline profiling to characterize layer sensitivity and token importance, enabling adaptive precision allocation under a fixed memory constraint. Guided by the profiled memory--accuracy trade-off, it automatically derives an effective precision allocation strategy without online allocation search, and applies the resulting policy during inference. Extensive experiments on reasoning and long-context benchmarks demonstrate that MultiAlloc consistently improves over layer-wise, token-wise, and recent multi-granularity KV cache quantization methods under matched memory budgets across diverse models, including Mistral, Llama, DeepSeek-Qwen, and QwQ.
items.title_zh: MultiAlloc：KV缓存量化的预算感知精度分配
items.summary_zh: 论文提出MultiAlloc框架，旨在解决在固定KV缓存内存预算下如何将有限的量化资源分配给异构精度保持策略的问题。该框架通过轻量级离线分析层敏感性和Token重要性，自适应地在逐层精度增强和逐Token保持之间分配资源，从而在推理和长上下文基准测试中持续优于现有方法。

items.title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Non-prefix KV cache reuse is a promising approach for improving inference efficiency in multi-agent systems as agents share the same context blocks. However, when agents have conflicting tasks, directly reusing non-prefix KV caches across agents can severely degrade model performance, causing up to a 90% drop. Existing remedies, including selective recomputation and offset-based calibration, recover a limited fraction of this loss. We argue that the problem lies not only in contaminated KV representations but also in the agent's difficulty interpreting reused context under its own instructions. To this end, we introduce LatentRemedy, which uses a few task-conditioned latent tokens to help the target agent leverage reused context without recomputing the shared block. Specifically, we use an MLP to map the last hidden state of the target prefix into a small number of latent tokens, which are placed after the reused KV block to interact with the shared context. To guide subsequent predictions toward the target task, we train the MLP through full-prefill distillation. Experiments show that LatentRemedy consistently outperforms existing reuse baselines on conflicting tasks while maintaining TTFT close to direct reuse as cache size grows. Code and data are available at https://github.com/chenzhwsysu57/kvreuse.
items.title_zh: LatentRemedy：多智能体系统中非前缀KV缓存重用的高效补救
items.summary_zh: 针对多智能体系统中因任务冲突直接重用非前缀KV缓存导致性能严重下降的问题，论文提出了LatentRemedy方法。该方法通过少量任务条件化潜变量Token帮助目标智能体利用共享上下文，在保持首字延迟接近直接重用的同时，显著优于现有的缓存重用基线。
